brief: UBS S&T rates desk note (16-Nov-2026). Asian equities sold off on tech-sector fears ahead of Nvidia's earnings this week and Microsoft news, with Nikkei -2.42%, Kospi -3.59%, Taiwan -6%, while Hong Kong/China H shares rose 0.5%; some analysts still recommend max overweight on global stocks on an intact AI capex cycle. Rates: TY futures stayed in a narrow range on a quiet session, with block selling in TYZ6/FVZ6, a 2s10s steepener, and a seller of TYF7 put spreads. China data came in weaker than expected (unemployment fell 5.2% to 5.1%, retail sales and industrial production both missed); UBS Economics says September's strength reflected front-loading and underlying growth momentum is weak, with administrative tightening offsetting loosening; CSI 300 fell just over 1%. Fed officials (Schmid, Jefferson, Williams) flagged persistent inflation risk from energy, durable goods, AI buildout spillover and healthcare costs, explicitly excluding labor market as a driver; the internal debate has shifted from whether to hike to the pace (Waller floated 50bp, Logan favors 25bp Dec/Jan, Hammack and Collins prefer gradual). Separately, UK electricity costs for businesses are forecast to rise ~13% by decade-end per Cornwall Insight, and BoE's Pill said the Bank has further to go and current market pricing of 100bp of hikes over 12 months is not outrageous.
